stories.title: David, the shepherd who wrote Psalm 23
stories.story: Before David was a king, he was the youngest son, sent out to watch sheep while his brothers got noticed. He knew what it was to protect something fragile in the dark. Later, through danger and seasons on the run, he wrote that God was his shepherd and stayed with him even in the darkest valley.

verses.text: Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.

stories.title: Joseph and his brothers
stories.story: Joseph's own brothers were jealous of him, so they threw him in a pit and sold him into slavery. He spent years as a slave and then in prison for something he didn't do. Over time God raised him up to lead Egypt. When a famine hit, the same brothers came to him for food, and Joseph chose to forgive them.

verses.text: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is today, to save many people alive.
Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

stories.title: Joseph forgotten in prison
stories.story: In prison, Joseph helped Pharaoh's cupbearer by explaining his dream, and asked only to be remembered. The cupbearer got out and forgot him for two more years. Then Pharaoh had a dream no one could explain, the cupbearer finally remembered, and Joseph went from prison to second in command in a single day.

verses.text: Let us not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.

stories.title: Peter walks on the water
stories.story: In the middle of a storm, the disciples saw Jesus walking toward their boat on the water. Peter asked to come to him, stepped out, and actually walked on the waves. Then he looked at the wind, got scared, and started to sink. He cried out, and Jesus reached out and caught him right away.

verses.text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

stories.title: Elijah under the broom tree
stories.story: Right after one of his biggest wins, Elijah was threatened and ran for his life. He sat under a tree in the desert and told God he'd had enough. God didn't lecture him. He let Elijah sleep, sent an angel with food, and let him rest again before the next step.

verses.text: Yahweh’s angel came again the second time, and touched him, and said, “Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you.”
“Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

stories.title: The son who came home
stories.story: Jesus told of a young man who took his inheritance early and wasted all of it. Broke and hungry, he decided to go home and beg to be a servant. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, ran to him, and threw a party. The father never made him earn his way back.

verses.text: “He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

stories.title: Zacchaeus makes it right
stories.story: Zacchaeus was a tax collector who had gotten rich by cheating people, and everyone knew it. When Jesus came to town, Zacchaeus climbed a tree just to see him. Jesus called him by name and went to his house. Zacchaeus was so changed that he promised to give half his wealth to the poor and pay back anyone he cheated four times over.

verses.text: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

stories.title: David's prayer after his worst failure
stories.story: King David abused his power, took another man's wife, and tried to cover it up in a terrible way. When the prophet Nathan confronted him, David didn't make excuses. He owned it, faced the consequences, and wrote Psalm 51, asking God for a clean heart.

verses.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

stories.title: Peter denies Jesus, then is restored
stories.story: Peter swore he would never abandon Jesus. That same night he denied even knowing him three times, then went out and wept. After the resurrection, Jesus found Peter by the sea, cooked him breakfast, and gave him three chances to say he loved him, one for each denial.

verses.text: It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

stories.title: Hannah prays for a child
stories.story: Hannah wanted a child more than anything, and another woman in the house mocked her for it year after year. She went to the temple and prayed so hard that the priest thought she was drunk. She poured out her heart honestly. In time she had a son, Samuel.

verses.text: I prayed for this child; and Yahweh has given me my petition which I asked of him.
Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.

stories.title: Ruth starts over
stories.story: Ruth lost her husband young. Her mother in law Naomi had lost everything too and told Ruth to go back home. Ruth refused to leave her. She moved to a strange land, worked in the fields to feed them both, and found a new family and future there.

verses.text: Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.

stories.title: Jesus weeps with Mary and Martha
stories.story: Jesus' close friend Lazarus got sick and died before Jesus arrived. His sisters Mary and Martha were heartbroken and asked why he hadn't come sooner. Jesus didn't rush past their pain. He stood at the tomb and wept with them, even knowing he was about to raise Lazarus to life.

verses.text: Jesus wept.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.

stories.title: Job loses everything
stories.story: Job was a good man who lost his wealth, his children, and his health one after another. His friends blamed him. Job was brutally honest with God about his pain and questions, and God did not condemn his honesty. In the end God met him, and Job's life was restored.

verses.text: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

stories.title: Moses says he's not good enough
stories.story: God called Moses to lead his people out of Egypt. Moses came up with excuse after excuse: no one will listen, I'm not a good speaker, send someone else. God didn't pick someone more confident. He promised to be with Moses and gave him his brother Aaron to help.

verses.text: Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.”

stories.title: Gideon hiding in the winepress
stories.story: Gideon was hiding, threshing wheat in a winepress so enemy raiders wouldn't see him. An angel showed up and called him a mighty man of valor. Gideon said his clan was the weakest and he was the least in his family. God used him anyway, with an army cut down to just 300.

verses.text: Yahweh’s angel appeared to him, and said to him, “Yahweh is with you, you mighty man of valor!”
He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.

stories.title: David faces Goliath
stories.story: A giant named Goliath taunted Israel's army for forty days, and every soldier was too scared to face him. David, a teenage shepherd bringing his brothers lunch, volunteered. He turned down the king's armor, used what he knew, a sling and stones, and trusted God with the rest.

verses.text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”

stories.title: Jesus calms the storm
stories.story: The disciples were crossing a lake when a huge storm hit and waves filled the boat. Jesus was asleep in the back. They woke him up shouting, "Don't you care that we're dying?" He stood up, spoke to the wind and waves, and everything went calm.

verses.text: He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

stories.title: Paul writes from prison
stories.story: Paul wrote his letter to the Philippians while under arrest. He had been rich in status and had also been hungry, beaten, and shipwrecked. From that place he wrote that he had learned to be content in plenty and in need, because Christ gave him strength.

verses.text: I know how to be humbled, and I know also how to abound. In everything and in all things I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need. I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

stories.title: Jonah runs the other way
stories.story: God told Jonah to go to Nineveh, and Jonah boarded a ship headed the opposite direction. A storm hit, he was thrown overboard, and a great fish swallowed him. From inside the fish he prayed. God gave him a second chance, and Jonah went.

verses.text: He said, “I called because of my affliction to Yahweh. He answered me. Out of the belly of Sheol I cried. You heard my voice.

stories.title: The woman at the well
stories.story: A Samaritan woman came to draw water at noon, likely to avoid the people who gossiped about her past. Jesus was there and asked her for a drink, breaking every social rule. He knew her whole story and still treated her with dignity. She ran back to town to tell the same people who had judged her.

verses.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

stories.title: Martha, worried about many things
stories.story: Jesus visited the home of Martha and Mary. Martha rushed around doing all the work while Mary sat and listened to Jesus. Frustrated, Martha asked Jesus to tell her sister to help. Jesus answered her gently and invited her to slow down too.

verses.text: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

stories.title: David refuses revenge on Saul
stories.story: King Saul was hunting David to kill him out of jealousy. One day Saul walked into the very cave where David was hiding. David's men told him this was his chance. David cut off a corner of Saul's robe but refused to harm him, and left justice to God.

verses.text: Don’t seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to God’s wrath. For it is written, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord.”
“Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath,

stories.title: Abraham leaves home
stories.story: God told Abram to leave his country, his relatives, and his father's house and go to a land God would show him later. He didn't get a map or a timeline. He packed up and went anyway, one step at a time.

verses.text: Now Yahweh said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.
Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.

stories.title: Jacob and Esau reunite
stories.story: Jacob cheated his brother Esau out of his blessing and fled for his life. Twenty years later he had to face him and was terrified. He sent gifts ahead and expected the worst. Instead Esau ran to meet him, hugged him, and they both wept.

verses.text: Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.

stories.title: Jesus alone in Gethsemane
stories.story: The night before the cross, Jesus asked his closest friends to stay awake and pray with him. They kept falling asleep. Alone and deeply distressed, he was honest with God about wanting another way, and still chose to trust him.

verses.text: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”

stories.title: Moses' mother lets go
stories.story: When Pharaoh ordered baby boys killed, Moses' mother hid him for three months. When she couldn't hide him any longer, she made a basket, placed him in the river, and had his sister watch. Pharaoh's daughter found him, and Moses' own mother ended up being paid to nurse him.

verses.text: He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.

stories.title: Thomas wants proof
stories.story: Thomas wasn't there when the risen Jesus first appeared, and he said he wouldn't believe without seeing the wounds himself. A week later Jesus came back, went straight to Thomas, and offered exactly what he asked for. No shame, just an invitation.

verses.text: Then he said to Thomas, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”
Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”

stories.title: Noah waits out the flood
stories.story: Noah built the ark when there wasn't a cloud in the sky, while people mocked him. Then he and his family were shut inside for over a year while the flood covered everything. It was long, cramped and uncertain. But God did not forget them, and the waters went down.

verses.text: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided.

stories.title: Sarah laughs at the promise
stories.story: God promised Abraham and Sarah a son, but they waited until they were far too old. When Sarah overheard the promise again, she laughed to herself. It sounded impossible. A year later she held her son Isaac, whose name means laughter.

verses.text: Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes round, and Sarah will have a son.”

stories.title: Hagar, the God who sees
stories.story: Hagar was a servant who was used and then mistreated, so she ran into the desert alone. By a spring of water, God met her there. She became the only person in scripture to give God a name: the God who sees me.

verses.text: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”

stories.title: Leah, the unloved wife
stories.story: Jacob loved Leah's sister Rachel and was tricked into marrying Leah first. Leah spent years hoping her husband would finally love her. With each son she named, you can hear her longing. By the fourth, she shifted her focus and said, this time I will praise the Lord. That son, Judah, became the line of King David and Jesus.

verses.text: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time will I praise Yahweh.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

stories.title: Esther speaks up
stories.story: Esther was a young Jewish woman who became queen, keeping her background secret. When a law was passed to wipe out her people, going to the king uninvited could cost her life. Her cousin told her maybe she was there for such a time as this. She fasted, then walked in anyway.

verses.text: For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”

stories.title: Daniel in the lions' den
stories.story: Daniel did his job so well that jealous officials looked for dirt on him and found none. So they tricked the king into a law against prayer, knowing Daniel would keep praying. He did, and was thrown to the lions. In the morning he walked out unharmed.

verses.text: My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me; because as before him innocence was found in me; and also before you, O king, I have done no harm.”

stories.title: Three friends and the furnace
stories.story: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refused to bow to the king's golden statue, even under threat of a blazing furnace. They said God could save them, and even if he didn't, they still wouldn't bow. They were thrown in, and the king saw a fourth figure walking with them in the fire.

verses.text: If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.”

stories.title: Nehemiah rebuilds the wall
stories.story: Nehemiah heard that Jerusalem's walls were still in ruins and wept. He got permission to go rebuild, organized the people, and kept working while critics mocked and threatened them. They finished the wall in just 52 days.

verses.text: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.”

stories.title: Naomi says call me bitter
stories.story: Naomi lost her husband and both sons in a foreign land. When she came home, she told people not to call her Naomi, which means pleasant, but Mara, which means bitter. God didn't reject her honesty. Through Ruth, her life was filled again, and she ended up holding a grandson.

verses.text: She said to them, “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara; for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

stories.title: The woman who touched his cloak
stories.story: A woman had been sick for twelve years. She spent everything on doctors and only got worse, and her condition left her cut off from others. She pushed through a crowd just to touch the edge of Jesus' cloak. He stopped everything to find her and called her daughter.

verses.text: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”

stories.title: Bartimaeus won't be quiet
stories.story: Bartimaeus was a blind man begging by the road. When he heard Jesus was passing, he shouted for him. The crowd told him to be quiet, so he shouted louder. Jesus stopped, called him over, and asked what he wanted.

verses.text: Jesus asked him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”

stories.title: Paul, pressed but not crushed
stories.story: Paul was beaten, shipwrecked, jailed, hungry and sleepless during his travels. Writing to friends in Corinth, he didn't pretend it was easy. He said he was hard pressed on every side, but never crushed, and never abandoned.

verses.text: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair; pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;

stories.title: Saul becomes Paul
stories.story: Saul hunted down and jailed Christians. On the road to Damascus, a blinding light stopped him, and Jesus spoke to him. Saul was changed. People were afraid of him at first because of his past, but he became Paul, who wrote much of the New Testament.

verses.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

stories.title: Paul and Silas sing at midnight
stories.story: Paul and Silas were beaten and locked in stocks for helping a girl. Instead of despairing, at midnight they prayed and sang while the other prisoners listened. An earthquake opened the doors, and the jailer and his whole family came to faith that night.

verses.text: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.

stories.title: Mary hears unexpected news
stories.story: Mary was a young engaged woman when an angel told her she would have a son. It would upend her plans and her reputation. She asked honest questions, then said yes.

verses.text: Mary said, “Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.” The angel departed from her.

stories.title: The woman they wanted to stone
stories.story: Religious leaders dragged a woman before Jesus, caught in adultery, and demanded she be stoned. Jesus said whoever had no sin could throw the first stone. One by one they walked away. He told her he didn't condemn her and to go and live differently.

verses.text: She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.”

stories.title: Five loaves and two fish
stories.story: Over five thousand people were hungry and the disciples had no way to feed them. A boy offered his small lunch of five loaves and two fish. It seemed pointless. Jesus gave thanks, and everyone ate with twelve baskets left over.

verses.text: “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?”

stories.title: Jesus welcomes the children
stories.story: Parents brought children to Jesus and the disciples tried to send them away as a waste of his time. Jesus was upset with the disciples, not the kids. He welcomed the children, took them in his arms, and blessed them.

verses.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation, and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.

stories.title: The one lost sheep
stories.story: Jesus told of a shepherd with a hundred sheep who lost one. He left the ninety nine to search until he found it, then carried it home on his shoulders and threw a celebration.

verses.text: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?

stories.title: Manna in the wilderness
stories.story: In the desert, Israel had no food, and God sent manna each morning. They could only gather enough for that day. If they hoarded it, it spoiled. They learned to trust God one day at a time.

verses.text: Give us today our daily bread.

stories.title: Joshua steps into Moses' shoes
stories.story: After Moses died, Joshua had to lead a whole nation into a land full of walled cities. He was following a legend. God told him again and again to be strong and courageous, and promised to go ahead of him.

verses.text: Yahweh himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”

stories.title: A letter to people stuck in exile
tags: somewhere i don't want to be
stories.story: God's people were carried off to Babylon and wanted out fast. Jeremiah sent them a letter saying to build houses, plant gardens and seek the good of the city, because it would be seventy years. In that same letter God promised a hope and a future.

verses.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.

stories.title: Solomon asks for wisdom
stories.story: When Solomon became king, he felt like a little child who didn't know what he was doing. God offered him anything. He didn't ask for money or long life. He asked for wisdom to lead well, and God gave it generously.

verses.text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach; and it will be given to him.

stories.title: The older brother's resentment
stories.story: When the younger son came home and got a party, his older brother refused to go in. He had worked faithfully for years and never got a celebration. The father went outside to him too, and reminded him that everything he had was already his.

verses.text: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.

stories.title: David grieves his son
stories.story: David's son Absalom turned against him and tried to take his throne. Even then, David told his soldiers to be gentle with him. When Absalom died, David didn't celebrate his victory. He wept as a father.

verses.text: The king was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate, and wept. As he went, he said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I had died for you, Absalom, my son, my son!”

stories.title: Paul and Barnabas split up
stories.story: Paul and Barnabas were close ministry partners until they argued so sharply over a young man named Mark that they went separate ways. Years later, Paul wrote asking for Mark to come because he was useful to him. Broken relationships can heal.

verses.text: Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.

stories.title: Elisha's servant sees the army
stories.story: Elisha's servant woke up to see an enemy army surrounding their city and panicked. Elisha calmly told him not to be afraid, then prayed for his eyes to be opened. The servant saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire around them.

verses.text: He answered, “Don’t be afraid; for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”

stories.title: Jesus tempted in the wilderness
stories.story: After forty days of fasting, Jesus was hungry and exhausted when the devil came to tempt him. Each time, Jesus answered with scripture. He knows what temptation feels like from the inside.

verses.text: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.

stories.title: The road to Emmaus
stories.story: Two followers of Jesus walked home after the crucifixion, crushed that their hopes were gone. A stranger joined them and explained the scriptures as they walked. Only when he broke bread with them did they realize it was Jesus, who had been with them the whole way.

verses.text: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us, while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”

stories.title: Fishing all night with nothing
stories.story: Peter and his partners fished all night and caught nothing. Jesus told them to go back out and try again. Peter was tired and skeptical but did it anyway. The nets filled so full they started to tear.

verses.text: Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night, and took nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.”

stories.title: Adam and Eve hide
stories.story: After Adam and Eve ate the fruit God told them not to, they felt ashamed and hid among the trees. They started blaming each other. God came looking for them anyway and called out, asking where they were. Even with consequences, he clothed them before they left the garden.

verses.text: Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”

stories.title: Cain's anger at his brother
stories.story: Cain was angry and jealous because God accepted his brother Abel's offering and not his. Before Cain acted, God came to him and warned him that anger was crouching at the door, but he could master it. Cain didn't listen, and his anger cost him everything.

verses.text: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”

stories.title: Jacob wrestles with God
stories.story: The night before facing the brother he had wronged, Jacob was alone and afraid. A man wrestled with him until daybreak. Jacob refused to let go until he was blessed. He walked away limping, with a new name, Israel, meaning one who struggles with God.

verses.text: The man said, “Let me go, for the day breaks.” Jacob said, “I won’t let you go, unless you bless me.”

stories.title: Joseph falsely accused
stories.story: Joseph worked his way up in Potiphar's house. When Potiphar's wife tried to seduce him, he refused and ran. She lied and said he attacked her, and he was thrown in prison. Even there, God was with him and he was put in charge.

verses.text: The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because Yahweh was with him; and that which he did, Yahweh made it prosper.

stories.title: Trapped at the Red Sea
stories.story: Israel had just escaped Egypt when they found themselves trapped with the sea in front and Pharaoh's army behind. The people panicked. Moses told them to stand still and watch. God split the sea, and they walked through on dry ground.

verses.text: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.”

stories.title: Moses tries to do it all
stories.story: Moses sat from morning to evening settling every problem for the whole nation by himself. His father in law Jethro watched and told him this wasn't good, he would wear himself out. He helped Moses share the load with other capable people.

verses.text: You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone.

stories.title: Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' arms
stories.story: During a battle, Israel won as long as Moses held his arms up. But his arms got tired. His friends Aaron and Hur sat him on a rock and held his arms up, one on each side, until sunset. They won together.

verses.text: But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.

stories.title: Moses loses his temper
stories.story: After years of complaints, the people grumbled again about water. Moses was told to speak to a rock, but in frustration he yelled at the people and struck it twice. Water still came out, but his outburst had real consequences. Even great leaders lose their cool.

verses.text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.

stories.title: Caleb at 85
stories.story: Caleb was one of only two scouts who trusted God when the others were afraid. He waited forty five years for his promise. At 85, he asked for the hardest hill country, saying he was as strong as the day he started.

verses.text: As yet I am as strong today as I was in the day that Moses sent me. As my strength was then, even so is my strength now for war, to go out and to come in.

stories.title: Rahab takes a risk
stories.story: Rahab was a prostitute in Jericho with a reputation everyone knew. When Israelite spies came, she hid them at great risk to herself. She and her family were saved, and she became part of the family line of King David and Jesus.

verses.text: By faith, Rahab the prostitute, didn’t perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies in peace.

stories.title: Deborah leads when others hesitate
stories.story: Deborah was a judge and prophet leading Israel. When she told the commander Barak that God would give him victory, he wouldn't go unless she went too. She went, and encouraged him at the key moment that God had already gone ahead of them.

verses.text: Deborah said to Barak, “Go; for this is the day in which Yahweh has delivered Sisera into your hand. Hasn’t Yahweh gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

stories.title: Young Samuel hears his name
stories.story: Samuel was a boy serving in the temple when he heard someone call his name in the night. Three times he ran to the priest Eli, thinking it was him. Eli realized it was God and told Samuel to answer, speak, your servant is listening.

verses.text: Yahweh came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel said, “Speak; for your servant hears.”

stories.title: David, the son no one invited
stories.story: Samuel came to anoint the next king from Jesse's sons. Jesse lined up seven of them and didn't even call David, the youngest, in from the fields. God rejected each tall, impressive son. He chose the one no one thought to invite.

verses.text: But Yahweh said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but Yahweh looks at the heart.”

stories.title: David and Jonathan
stories.story: Jonathan was the king's son and should have been David's rival. Instead they became loyal friends. Jonathan protected David even from his own father. When they had to part, they wept together, and David never forgot him.

verses.text: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

stories.title: David at Ziklag
stories.story: David and his men came home to find their town burned and their families taken. His own men were so grieved they talked about stoning him. At his lowest point, David found strength in God, then went and recovered everything.

verses.text: David was greatly distressed; for the people spoke of stoning him, because the souls of all the people were grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters; but David strengthened himself in Yahweh his God.

stories.title: Mephibosheth at the king's table
stories.story: Mephibosheth was Jonathan's son, disabled in both feet since childhood, living in a remote place. He called himself a dead dog. King David sought him out, gave back his family's land, and gave him a permanent seat at the royal table.

verses.text: David said to him, “Don’t be afraid; for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You will eat bread at my table continually.”

stories.title: Saul's jealousy
stories.story: When the women sang that Saul had killed thousands but David tens of thousands, King Saul was eaten up with jealousy. From that day he watched David with suspicion. His envy slowly consumed his peace and his reign.

verses.text: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.

stories.title: Abigail the peacemaker
stories.story: Abigail's husband Nabal insulted David and his men, and David set out for revenge. Abigail quickly gathered food, rode out, and humbly talked David down. Her wisdom stopped bloodshed and kept David from a decision he would regret.

verses.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

stories.title: The widow's last meal
stories.story: During a famine, a widow was gathering sticks to cook one last meal for herself and her son. Elijah asked her to make him bread first and promised her flour and oil would not run out. She trusted him, and they didn't, day after day.

verses.text: The jar of meal didn’t run out, and the jar of oil did not fail, according to Yahweh’s word, which he spoke by Elijah.

stories.title: Elijah and the quiet whisper
stories.story: Elijah stood on a mountain waiting for God. A powerful wind tore the rocks, then an earthquake, then a fire, but God wasn't in any of them. Then came a gentle whisper, and that was where God spoke.

verses.text: After the earthquake a fire passed; but Yahweh was not in the fire. After the fire, there was a still small voice.

stories.title: The widow and the jars of oil
stories.story: A widow's creditors were coming to take her two sons as payment for debt. All she had was a little oil. Elisha told her to borrow every empty jar she could and start pouring. The oil kept flowing until the last jar was full, enough to pay the debt and live on.

verses.text: Then she came and told the man of God. He said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt; and you and your sons live on the rest.”

stories.title: Naaman and the muddy river
stories.story: Naaman was a powerful army commander with a skin disease. Elisha told him to wash seven times in the Jordan River. Naaman was insulted, it was too simple and too muddy. His servants talked him into it, and he was healed.

verses.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

stories.title: Hezekiah gets bad news
stories.story: King Hezekiah was told he was going to die from his illness. He turned his face to the wall and prayed, weeping. Before the prophet even left the palace, God sent him back with a new message: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears.

verses.text: “Turn back, and tell Hezekiah the prince of my people, ‘Yahweh, the God of David your father, says, “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day, you will go up to Yahweh’s house.

stories.title: Jehoshaphat doesn't know what to do
stories.story: Three armies were marching on King Jehoshaphat, and he was afraid. He gathered the people and prayed honestly: we have no power against this, and we don't know what to do, but our eyes are on you. They sent singers out ahead of the army, and the enemy fell apart.

verses.text: Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”

stories.title: The psalmist talks to his own soul
stories.story: The writer of Psalm 42 was far from home, crying day and night while people asked where his God was. He remembered better days. Then he did something brave: he talked back to his own sadness and told his soul to hope in God.

verses.text: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him, the saving help of my countenance, and my God.

stories.title: Isaiah says here I am
stories.story: Isaiah saw a vision of God's glory and was overwhelmed by his own flaws. He said he was ruined. God cleansed him, then asked who would go for him. Isaiah, just forgiven, said, here I am, send me.

verses.text: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”

stories.title: Jeremiah says I'm too young
stories.story: When God called Jeremiah to be a prophet, his first answer was that he was only a youth and didn't know how to speak. God told him not to say that, promised to be with him, and put his words in Jeremiah's mouth.

verses.text: But Yahweh said to me, “Don’t say, ‘I am a child;’ for you must go to whomever I send you, and you must say whatever I command you.

stories.title: The potter remakes the clay
stories.story: God sent Jeremiah to watch a potter at work. The pot the potter was making got spoiled in his hands. He didn't throw the clay away. He reshaped it into a new pot, and God said he could do the same with his people.

verses.text: When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.

stories.title: The valley of dry bones
stories.story: God showed Ezekiel a valley full of dry bones and asked if they could live. Ezekiel said only God knew. God told him to speak to the bones. They rattled together, grew muscle and skin, and breath came into them. They stood up as a great army.

verses.text: Thus says the Lord Yahweh to these bones: “Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and you will live.

stories.title: Habakkuk asks God why
stories.story: Habakkuk looked at violence and injustice around him and asked God how long he would let it go on. He argued, waited, and listened. By the end, nothing around him had changed yet, but he decided he would still trust and rejoice in God.

verses.text: For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines; the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food; the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!

stories.title: John the Baptist doubts in prison
stories.story: John the Baptist had boldly announced Jesus. Later, sitting in prison, he sent friends to ask Jesus if he was really the one. Jesus didn't scold him. He sent back evidence of what he was doing, then praised John to the crowd.

verses.text: and said to him, “Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?”

stories.title: The centurion's faith
stories.story: A Roman officer came to Jesus because his servant was paralyzed and suffering. When Jesus offered to come, the centurion said he wasn't worthy and asked Jesus to just say the word. Jesus was amazed at his faith, and the servant was healed that hour.

verses.text: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

stories.title: Jairus and his daughter
stories.story: Jairus begged Jesus to come heal his dying daughter. On the way, Jesus stopped to help someone else, and messengers came saying it was too late. Jesus turned to Jairus and told him not to be afraid, only believe. He went to the house and raised the girl up.

verses.text: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”

stories.title: Friends lower him through the roof
stories.story: A paralyzed man's friends carried him to see Jesus, but the house was packed. So they climbed on the roof, dug a hole, and lowered him down. Jesus saw their faith, forgave the man, and healed him.

verses.text: Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”

stories.title: The man by the pool for 38 years
stories.story: A man had been disabled for 38 years, lying by a pool people believed could heal. Every time, someone else got there first, and no one helped him. Jesus asked if he wanted to get well, then told him to pick up his mat and walk. He did.

verses.text: When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?” The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.”

stories.title: Jesus touches the leper
stories.story: A man with leprosy was forced to live apart from everyone, and no one would touch him. He knelt before Jesus and said, if you are willing, you can make me clean. Jesus was moved with compassion, reached out, touched him, and healed him.

verses.text: Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”

stories.title: The widow's two coins
stories.story: Jesus watched people put money into the temple offering. The rich gave big amounts. Then a poor widow dropped in two tiny coins. Jesus told his disciples she gave more than anyone, because she gave all she had.

verses.text: He called his disciples to himself, and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,

stories.title: Nicodemus comes at night
stories.story: Nicodemus was a respected religious leader with real questions about Jesus, so he came quietly at night. Jesus didn't turn him away. He talked with him honestly and told him how much God loved the world.

verses.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

stories.title: The woman who washed his feet
stories.story: At a dinner party, a woman known for her sinful life came in, wept over Jesus' feet, dried them with her hair, and poured perfume on them. The host judged her. Jesus defended her and said her many sins were forgiven, because she loved much.

verses.text: Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.”

stories.title: The rich young man
stories.story: A wealthy young man ran up to Jesus asking what he needed to do. He had kept the rules his whole life. Jesus looked at him with love and invited him to let go of his wealth and follow him. The man walked away sad, because he had much.

verses.text: Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”

stories.title: The good Samaritan
stories.story: Jesus told of a man beaten and left on the road. A priest and a temple worker walked past. Then a Samaritan, from a group the Jews looked down on, stopped, bandaged him, and paid for his care. Jesus said to go and do the same.

verses.text: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,

stories.title: How many times do I forgive
stories.story: Peter asked Jesus how many times he had to forgive someone, offering seven as generous. Jesus said seventy times seven, then told a story about a servant forgiven a huge debt who refused to forgive a small one.

verses.text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.

stories.title: The widow who kept knocking
stories.story: Jesus told of a widow who kept coming to an unfair judge demanding justice. He ignored her for a long time but finally gave in because she wouldn't stop. Jesus said if even an unjust judge responds, how much more will God, who loves you.

verses.text: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up,

stories.title: The servant who buried his talent
stories.story: A master gave three servants money to manage. Two invested it and doubled it. The third was afraid, so he buried his in the ground. Jesus used this story to show that God wants us to use what we've been given, not hide it out of fear.

verses.text: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

stories.title: Jesus washes their feet
stories.story: At the last supper, Jesus got up, wrapped a towel around himself, and washed his disciples' feet, the job of the lowest servant. He even washed the feet of Judas, who he knew would betray him. Then he told them to do the same for each other.

verses.text: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.

stories.title: Stephen forgives his attackers
stories.story: Stephen was a young leader full of grace who was falsely accused and dragged before the council. After he spoke, the crowd turned on him. As he was dying, he prayed for God not to hold it against them.

verses.text: He kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” When he had said this, he fell asleep.

stories.title: Paul's shipwreck
stories.story: Paul was a prisoner on a ship caught in a storm for two weeks. Everyone gave up hope. Paul stood up and told them to take courage, because God had told him they would lose the ship but every life would be saved. The ship broke apart, and all 276 people made it to shore.

verses.text: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

stories.title: Paul encourages timid Timothy
stories.story: Timothy was young, prone to worry, and leading a difficult church. Paul, his mentor, wrote to remind him of his gift and encourage him not to let fear rule him. God's Spirit is not a spirit of fear.

verses.text: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.

stories.title: Onesimus goes back
stories.story: Onesimus ran away from his master Philemon and may have taken from him. He met Paul and was changed. Paul sent him back with a letter asking Philemon to welcome him as a brother, and offered to pay anything Onesimus owed.

verses.text: who once was useless to you, but now is useful to you and to me.

stories.title: John exiled on Patmos
stories.story: John, now old, was exiled alone on a small island for his faith. There God gave him a vision of the future, including a new heaven and earth where every tear is wiped away and pain is gone for good.

verses.text: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.”

stories.title: Mary Magdalene at the empty tomb
stories.story: Mary Magdalene came to the tomb early and found it empty. She stood outside crying, thinking someone had taken Jesus' body. A man she thought was the gardener asked why she was weeping. Then he said her name, and she knew it was Jesus.

verses.text: Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!”

stories.title: The disciples behind locked doors
stories.story: After the crucifixion, the disciples hid behind locked doors, afraid they would be next. Jesus didn't wait for them to be brave. He came and stood among them and said, peace be with you.

verses.text: When therefore it was evening, on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”

stories.title: A prayer at the well for Isaac's wife
stories.story: Abraham sent his servant on a long journey to find a wife for his son Isaac. At a well, the servant prayed for God to guide him, and before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her water jar and showed him kindness. She agreed to go back with him. Isaac married Rebekah, he loved her, and she comforted him after his mother's death.

verses.text: Also delight yourself in Yahweh, and he will give you the desires of your heart.

stories.title: The wine runs out at a wedding in Cana
stories.story: At a wedding in Cana, the wine ran out before the celebration was over. Jesus' mother told him, and told the servants to do whatever he said. Jesus had them fill six large stone jars with water, and it became excellent wine. The man in charge of the feast didn't even know where it came from. It was the first sign Jesus did.

verses.text: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.”

stories.title: The one who came back to say thank you
stories.story: Ten men with leprosy called out to Jesus from a distance, asking for mercy. He sent them to show themselves to the priests, and on the way they were healed. Only one of them, a Samaritan, came back, praising God loudly and falling at Jesus' feet to thank him. Jesus asked where the other nine were, and told the man his faith had made him well.

verses.text: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.

stories.title: David dances with all his might
stories.story: When the ark of God was brought into Jerusalem, King David danced before the Lord with all his might while the people shouted and sounded trumpets. His wife Michal watched from a window and despised him for it. David told her he was celebrating before the Lord, and that he would gladly look even more humble than that.

verses.text: David danced before Yahweh with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.
You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,

stories.title: Miriam leads a song after the Red Sea
stories.story: After the Israelites crossed the Red Sea on dry ground and were finally free from Egypt, Miriam the prophetess picked up a tambourine. All the women followed her with tambourines and dancing, and she led them in a song praising God for rescuing them. After years of slavery and a terrifying escape, they stopped to celebrate what God had done.

verses.text: Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.

stories.title: Daniel, far from home in Babylon
stories.story: As young men, Daniel and his friends were taken from Jerusalem to Babylon and put through three years of training for the king's service. They were given new names and food from the king's table, but Daniel asked to eat vegetables and drink water instead. After a ten day test, they looked healthier than the others. God gave them knowledge and understanding, and at the end of their training they stood out above everyone.

verses.text: Now as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.

stories.title: Daniel asks for time and prays with friends
stories.story: King Nebuchadnezzar demanded that his wise men tell him both his dream and what it meant, or they would all be put to death. Daniel asked the king for time, then went home and asked his friends to pray with him. That night God showed Daniel the answer, and Daniel praised God before going back to the king.

verses.text: I thank you, and praise you, you God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the king’s matter.”
I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth.

stories.title: Joseph mourns his father
stories.story: When his father Jacob died, Joseph fell on his face, wept over him, and kissed him. Even as a powerful leader in Egypt, he stopped to grieve. He kept his promise to bury his father in the family grave in Canaan, and a large company traveled with him. They mourned for seven days before returning home.

verses.text: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.

stories.title: Jacob and the boss who kept changing the deal
stories.story: Jacob worked for his uncle Laban for twenty years. Laban tricked him more than once and changed his wages ten times. Jacob kept working through the heat of the day and the cold of the night. In the end God saw how Jacob had been treated, blessed his work, and made a way for him to leave.

verses.text: Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”

stories.title: The man thrown out after Jesus healed him
tags: parents didn't stand up for me
stories.story: Jesus healed a man who had been blind from birth. Instead of celebrating, the religious leaders questioned him again and again, and even his parents were too afraid to stand up for him. When he kept telling the truth, the leaders threw him out. Jesus heard about it, went and found him, and the man believed.

verses.text: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
When my father and my mother forsake me, then Yahweh will take me up.

stories.title: When Jesus' own family didn't understand
stories.story: Crowds pressed around Jesus so much that he and his disciples couldn't even eat, and people close to him went to take charge of him, saying he was out of his mind. Then his mother and brothers came and sent for him. Jesus looked at the people sitting around him and called them his mother and brothers. He said whoever does God's will is his family.

verses.text: For whoever does the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.”
God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.

stories.title: Jesus is rejected in his hometown
stories.story: Jesus went back to Nazareth, where he grew up, and read from Isaiah in the synagogue. At first people spoke well of him, then they began asking whether he was just Joseph's son. He told them no prophet is accepted in his hometown. They became furious and tried to throw him off a cliff, but he walked right through the crowd and went on his way.

verses.text: He said, “Most certainly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
But he, passing through the middle of them, went his way.

stories.title: David sleeps while on the run
stories.story: When his son Absalom rose up against him, King David had to flee Jerusalem. Many people said God would not rescue him. David wrote Psalm 3 during that time, saying that he lay down and slept and woke up again, because the Lord was holding him up.

verses.text: I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for Yahweh sustains me.
In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.

stories.title: Simeon holds the promise he waited for
stories.story: Simeon lived in Jerusalem, and God had promised him that he would not die before he saw the Messiah. When Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus to the temple, Simeon took him in his arms and praised God. He said he could now go in peace, because he had seen God's salvation with his own eyes.

verses.text: “Now you are releasing your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation,

stories.title: Peter pulls back out of fear of people
stories.story: In Antioch, Peter used to eat with the non-Jewish believers. But when certain people arrived, he pulled away and stopped eating with them, because he was afraid of what that group would think. Others followed his example. Paul confronted him face to face, because his fear of people was pulling him away from what he knew was true.

verses.text: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I wouldn’t be a servant of Christ.
The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in Yahweh is kept safe.

stories.title: Peter asks, what about him?
stories.story: After Jesus told Peter what his own future would hold, Peter turned, saw John, and asked what would happen to him. Jesus answered that John's path was not Peter's concern. Peter's part was simply to follow Jesus himself.

verses.text: Jesus said to him, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”
But let each man examine his own work, and then he will have reason to boast in himself, and not in someone else.

stories.title: The Teacher searches for meaning
stories.story: The Teacher, a king in Jerusalem, set out to find what makes life worth living. He tried pleasure, great building projects, wealth, and wisdom, and still found it all felt like chasing the wind. At the end of his search, he concluded that what matters is to honor God and keep his commandments.

verses.text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.

stories.title: Twelve stones from the Jordan
stories.story: When the Israelites crossed the Jordan River into the land God had promised, God told Joshua to have twelve men each carry a stone from the middle of the river. They set the stones up as a memorial. When their children later asked what the stones meant, they would tell how God brought them across.

verses.text: Joshua said to the people, “Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow Yahweh will do wonders among you.”
Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “Yahweh helped us until now.”

stories.title: Jeremiah tries to quit
stories.story: Jeremiah was mocked all day long because of the messages God gave him to speak. He was so worn down that he decided he would stop speaking for God altogether. But he found he couldn't hold it in; it burned inside him like fire. He held on to the truth that the Lord was with him.

verses.text: If I say, I will not make mention of him, or speak any more in his name, then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I can’t.

But Yahweh is with me as an awesome mighty one. Therefore my persecutors will stumble, and they won’t prevail. They will be utterly disappointed, because they have not dealt wisely, even with an everlasting dishonor which will never be forgotten.

stories.title: Isaac keeps digging wells
stories.story: Isaac dug wells for his household and flocks, but local herdsmen argued and claimed the water each time. Instead of fighting, Isaac moved on and dug another well. Finally he dug one that no one quarreled over, and he named it Rehoboth, saying the Lord had made room for them.

verses.text: He left that place, and dug another well. They didn’t argue over that one. He called it Rehoboth. He said, “For now Yahweh has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.

stories.title: Esther, raised by her cousin
stories.story: Esther lost both her father and her mother when she was young. Her cousin Mordecai took her in and raised her as his own daughter. That orphaned girl grew up to become queen, and she helped save her whole people.

verses.text: A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.

stories.title: No room for them in Bethlehem
stories.story: Mary and Joseph had to travel to Bethlehem for a census while Mary was about to give birth. When they arrived, there was no room for them in the inn. Mary gave birth to Jesus, wrapped him, and laid him in a manger, a feeding trough, because there was no other place for them.

verses.text: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

stories.title: Jesus' family flees to Egypt
stories.story: After Jesus was born, an angel warned Joseph in a dream that King Herod was trying to kill the child. Joseph got up in the night and took Mary and Jesus to Egypt. They lived there as foreigners until Herod died, then came back and settled in Nazareth.

verses.text: He arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt,
Yahweh preserves the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and widow, but the way of the wicked he turns upside down.

stories.title: Jesus eats at Levi's house
stories.story: Levi was a tax collector, the kind of person others avoided. Jesus saw him sitting at his tax booth and invited him to follow, and Levi got up and followed him. Then Jesus ate at Levi's house with other tax collectors and sinners. When the religious leaders complained, Jesus said it is the sick who need a doctor.

verses.text: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.

stories.title: Jonah sulks under a plant
stories.story: After God showed mercy to the city of Nineveh, Jonah was furious, because he had wanted the city punished. He went outside the city and sat to see what would happen, and God made a plant grow to give him shade. When the plant withered, Jonah was angry again. God asked him whether it was right to be so angry, and reminded him how much he cared about the people of that city.

verses.text: Yahweh said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
Yahweh is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.

stories.title: David's song: God knows me completely
stories.story: David wrote a song about how completely God knows him. He said God saw him being formed before he was born, knows his thoughts before he speaks, and is with him even in the dark. There was nowhere he could go that was out of God's reach.

verses.text: For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my mother’s womb. I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.

stories.title: David's prayer: How long?
stories.story: David asked God again and again, how long? He felt forgotten, like God had hidden his face, and sorrow filled his heart every day. By the end of the same short psalm, he chose to trust in God's loving kindness, and said he would sing because God had been good to him.

verses.text: How long, Yahweh? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
But I trust in your loving kindness. My heart rejoices in your salvation.

stories.title: The years the locusts ate
stories.story: In Joel's day, waves of locusts swept through the land and ate everything, leaving the fields and vines bare. The people had nothing left. God called them to come back to him with all their heart, and promised to restore the years the locusts had eaten.

verses.text: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.

stories.title: Elijah by the brook that dried up
stories.story: During a long drought, God sent Elijah to stay by the brook Cherith. Ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and evening, and he drank from the brook. After a while the brook dried up, and God sent him on to a new place where he would be provided for.

verses.text: You shall drink from the brook. I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?

stories.title: Anna, the widow at the temple
stories.story: Anna was a prophetess whose husband died after only seven years of marriage. For many years afterward, until she was very old, she stayed at the temple worshiping God night and day. When she saw the baby Jesus, she gave thanks to God and spoke about him to everyone who was waiting for redemption.

verses.text: Coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of him to all those who were looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.

stories.title: Mary and Joseph search for twelve year old Jesus
stories.story: When Jesus was twelve, his family went to Jerusalem for Passover. On the way home, Mary and Joseph realized he wasn't with them, and they searched anxiously for three days. They finally found him in the temple, listening to the teachers and asking questions. They didn't understand his answer, but Mary kept all these things in her heart, and Jesus kept growing in wisdom.

verses.text: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.

stories.title: No one stood with Paul
stories.story: Near the end of his life, Paul wrote to Timothy that at his first hearing in court, no one came to stand with him; everyone deserted him. He asked that it not be held against them. He said the Lord stood with him and gave him strength.

verses.text: At my first defense, no one came to help me, but all left me. May it not be held against them. But the Lord stood by me, and strengthened me, that through me the message might be fully proclaimed, and that all the Gentiles might hear; and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.

stories.title: Come away and rest a while
stories.story: The disciples came back from a busy mission and told Jesus everything they had done. So many people were coming and going that they didn't even have time to eat. Jesus told them to come away with him to a quiet place and rest a while, and they went off together in a boat.

verses.text: He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
“Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.”

stories.title: Nathan tells David the hard truth
stories.story: After King David did something terribly wrong and tried to cover it up, God sent the prophet Nathan to him. Nathan told David a story about a rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, and David was furious at the rich man. Then Nathan told David that he was that man. David admitted he had sinned, and Nathan told him the Lord had put away his sin.

verses.text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him, who is the head, Christ;

stories.title: The woman who searched for one coin
stories.story: Jesus told about a woman who had ten silver coins and lost one. She lit a lamp, swept the house, and searched carefully until she found it. Then she called her friends and neighbors to celebrate with her. Jesus said there is joy like that in heaven over one person who turns back to God.

verses.text: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”

stories.title: David grieves his best friend
stories.story: When David heard that his closest friend Jonathan had been killed in battle, he tore his clothes, wept, and fasted until evening. Then he wrote a song of mourning for him. He said Jonathan had been very dear to him, and he grieved deeply.

verses.text: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. You have been very pleasant to me. Your love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

stories.title: David stops hiding
stories.story: David wrote about a time when he kept his wrongdoing hidden. While he stayed silent, he felt worn down day and night, as if his strength were drying up. When he finally confessed to God and stopped hiding, he found forgiveness and relief.

verses.text: I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn’t hide my iniquity. I said, I will confess my transgressions to Yahweh, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah.
Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered.

stories.title: A proud king is humbled
stories.story: King Nebuchadnezzar walked on his palace roof and boasted about the great city he had built by his own power. Right then he lost his kingdom and his sanity, and lived out in the fields like an animal. When he finally looked up to heaven, his understanding came back, and he praised God, saying God is able to humble those who walk in pride.

verses.text: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven; for all his works are truth, and his ways justice; and those who walk in pride he is able to abase.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

stories.title: Elisha leaves the plow behind
stories.story: Elisha was plowing a field with twelve pairs of oxen when Elijah passed by and threw his cloak over him, calling him to follow. Elisha asked to say goodbye to his father and mother first. Then he slaughtered his oxen, cooked the meat using the wood of his plow, gave it to the people, and went to follow Elijah.

verses.text: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

stories.title: Elizabeth's neighbors rejoice with her
stories.story: Elizabeth had been unable to have children for many years. When she finally gave birth to a son, her neighbors and relatives heard how the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her. Everyone wondered what this child would grow up to be.

verses.text: Her neighbors and her relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy towards her, and they rejoiced with her.
Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation, nor turning shadow.

stories.title: Paul finds the doors closed
stories.story: Paul and his companions tried to go into the province of Asia, and then into Bithynia, but the Spirit kept them from going. With those doors closed, they went down to Troas. There Paul had a vision in the night of a man from Macedonia asking for help, and they set out, concluding that God had called them there.

verses.text: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”

stories.title: Barnabas believes in Saul
stories.story: After Saul met Jesus, he tried to join the disciples in Jerusalem, but they were all afraid of him and didn't believe he had really changed. Barnabas took him to the apostles and told them how Saul had seen the Lord and preached boldly. Because one person stood up for him, Saul was welcomed in.

verses.text: Therefore exhort one another, and build each other up, even as you also do.
